steps.text: EARLY EVENING — It is half past six. You are at home, waiting to hear from {{name:lena}} after work.
I'm out. Getting our food, then coming straight over ❤️
How was work?
Busy enough that I didn't have time to worry about the presentation
I've got our sandwiches. See you in a little while
See you soon
A LITTLE LATER — {{name:lena}} arrives at your place with her notes and a bag of food. You greet her with a kiss, put the sandwiches in the kitchen and sit together at the table.
Okay. I need you to pretend you're not my boyfriend for ten minutes.
That's a difficult opening request.
An ordinary person in the audience, then. Who isn't allowed to kiss me until I'm finished.
Understood. The floor is yours.

{{name:lena}} opens her slides and starts her presentation. You listen as she explains how quality, convenience and personal service can encourage customers to return. Halfway through, she pauses and looks down at her notes.
This is where I always get stuck.
Can I ask something?
Yes. That's what you're here for.
If two places sell the same thing for the same price, what makes someone choose one over the other?
The experience. Whether it's easy to shop there, whether the staff help you...
That makes sense. Why not start that section with the question?
Instead of that long definition?
Yeah. Give me an example first, then explain it.
Wait. Let me write that down.
She adds the question to her notes and tries the section again, using two neighbourhood cafes as an example. This time, she gets through it without stopping.
I followed all of that.
Was it too simple?
No. I understood what you meant. Then the definition made more sense.
Okay. That's actually helpful.
Actually?
Don't ruin your good work.
20 MINUTES LATER — {{name:lena}} finishes the presentation, checks the time and closes her laptop. You ask one last question about her conclusion, and she answers without looking at her notes.
That felt much better.
You looked up more on the second try, too.
You were looking right at me every time I did.
You asked for an attentive audience.
I did. And I liked having one.
Thank you for taking it seriously.
{{name:lena}} moves beside your chair and bends down to kiss you
You were waiting for me to close that laptop, weren't you?
I was following the rules. No kissing until you finished.
Very disciplined of you.
Can I stop pretending I'm just someone in the audience now?
Please do.
You didn't need a presentation to have a reason to come over.
I know. But I did need to practise it.
And I wanted to spend the evening with you. This worked out nicely.
It did.

25 MINUTES LATER — After eating, you move to the sofa. {{name:lena}} sits close beside you, leaving room for your recovering leg. Your arm settles around her shoulders, and she turns toward you for another kiss.
Much better than the table.
The table wasn't that bad.
I couldn't sit like this there.
Come here, then.
Your hand is wandering.
You can tell me to stop.
I didn't say stop. Higher.
And the other one?
You can have that too. Under. I already decided.
You're making it very difficult to keep the evening polite.
The presentation is over. I don't need polite.
My turn too.
You don't have to.
I know. I want to. Open your jeans.
Tell me if that's too much.
It isn't.
There. That was the point.
You look very pleased with yourself.
I am. You can thank me later
25 MINUTES LATER — After cleaning up, she nestles against you
Comfortable?
Yes. Are you?
Very.
Then stop moving away to talk.
I was going to ask about your day.
How was university?
Fine. Though I spent lunch rewriting that introduction instead of eating properly.
So the sandwich was important.
Very important. Thank you for helping with the presentation before I got distracted.
You did most of the work before you came here.
You helped me say it out loud. That's the part I needed.
20 MINUTES LATER — Later, {{name:lena}} checks the time and gathers her notes. She puts her laptop away, picks up both bags and joins you by the door.
Both bags accounted for?
Yes. I'm leaving you with absolutely no administrative reason to invite me back.
I think I'll manage without one.
I was hoping you would.
{{name:lena}} sets the bags down for a moment and steps back toward you. She kisses you goodbye, one hand resting on your shoulder while your arm wraps around her waist.
Okay. Now I'm really going.
Text me when you get home.
I will. Love you.
Love you too.
{{name:lena}} picks up both bags and leaves. You tidy the table and settle in for the rest of the evening.
20 MINUTES LATER — {{name:lena}} IS HOME
Home ❤️ Both bags made it
Excellent. Any forgotten notes?
No. I checked twice
And I tried that difficult section again while I was unpacking
How did it go?
Without looking down once 😌
That's good. Keep the question at the start
Already written in very large letters
Everything packed away. I'm done studying for tonight
You earned the break
Thank you for tonight. The useful part AND the part on the sofa ❤️
I enjoyed both
So did I. Especially the part after I closed the laptop
Now I'm getting ready for bed before I start rehearsing the whole thing again
Goodnight, love
Goodnight ❤️
